fields.title: Horse Genetics
fields.short_description: No photos—just genetics, no compromises. A quiz for horse lovers who enjoy short genetics problems and want to understand the inheritance behind equine coat colors.
fields.intro: No photos—just genetics, no compromises. A quiz for horse lovers who enjoy short genetics problems and want to understand the inheritance behind equine coat colors.

fields.question: What coat colors can the foals of a cremello horse have?
fields.explanation: Cremello results from two Cream alleles at the cream locus, regardless of the base color. Therefore, every offspring of such a horse will inherit a Cream allele and have a cream-dilute coat color.

fields.question: What coat colors can two black horses produce?
fields.explanation: A black horse can carry the recessive chestnut allele, so in addition to black foals, the pair can also produce chestnut offspring.

fields.question: Can two buckskin horses produce a cremello foal?
fields.explanation: Buckskin horses are heterozygous at the cream locus, while cremellos are homozygous: Cn + Cn → CC, Cn, Cn, nn. The probability is 25%.

fields.question: What coat color does one Cream allele produce on a chestnut base?
fields.explanation: Cremello results from two Cream alleles on any base color; buckskin is one Cream allele on a bay base; palomino is one Cream allele on a chestnut base; and red dun does not involve the Cream allele at all.

fields.question: What coat colors will the foals of two cremello horses have?
fields.explanation: Both parents have two Cream alleles, so they can produce only offspring with the same genotype: CC + CC → CC.

fields.question: Can a frame overo stallion be bred to a frame overo mare?
fields.explanation: A frame overo horse is always heterozygous at the frame overo locus, because homozygosity causes lethal white overo syndrome. Affected foals are completely white and die within hours or days of birth because of intestinal obstruction.

fields.question: What is the coat color of a horse with genotype EeAaCn?
fields.explanation: A dominant allele at the Extension locus allows black pigment; a dominant allele at the Agouti locus restricts that pigment to the points, producing bay; and one Cream allele dilutes bay to buckskin.

fields.question: What is the coat color of a horse with genotype eeAaCn?
fields.explanation: Two recessive alleles at the Extension locus produce chestnut, regardless of the Agouti genotype, and one Cream allele dilutes chestnut to palomino.

fields.question: Can a black mare produce a bay foal by a black stallion?
fields.explanation: Black horses do not have a dominant allele at the Agouti locus; if they did, they would be bay. Since neither parent has the dominant bay-producing allele, they cannot produce a bay foal.

fields.question: Which genotypes produce a palomino coat?

fields.question: Which genotypes produce a smoky black coat?

fields.explanation: Because the horse is homozygous at the gray locus (GG), every foal will inherit a dominant gray allele (G), so all of them will turn gray.

fields.question: Which allele can a black horse carry without showing it?
fields.explanation: The dominant Agouti allele (A) would make a black horse bay; dun (D) would make it grullo; gray (G) would make it turn gray; and silver (Z) would produce silver black. The chestnut allele (e), however, is recessive and can remain hidden in the presence of the dominant Extension allele (E) responsible for a black base.
